project.objective: Discriminate between two rival hypotheses on the specified finite grids. H_low predicts the low interval alone contains a point reaching the cutoff. H_high predicts the high interval alone does. Both or neither would refute both. Use actual measurements. Compare two acquisition methods on the qualifying interval: the unique quadratic interpolant and piecewise-linear interpolation of that interval's three measured coordinates. When the follow-up controller catalog arrives, evaluate each method on its permitted coordinates and choose its maximum. Measure the two choices in one new grid, with candidate IDs 'quadratic' and 'linear' identifying the method, then close. Cite the scores. In the final decision compare the held-out measurements and give the limits of the comparison. Preserve contrary evidence.

rubric.frozen_before_dispatch: Record the SHA-256 of this entire case and of the grader before starting any Job. Score only observed evidence. Missing or invalid measurements do not establish a negative result.
rubric.relative_hypotheses: Verify the two measured outcomes, the prospective cutoff, preservation of both scientific settlements, and the interpretation that only H_high survives this finite test.
rubric.source_use: Both independent review and planner cite the exact two source artifacts against actual research evidence. Accept the prospective catalog. Reject or quarantine the archival score because the current measured x=1 score contradicts it. The catalog constrains only new coordinates.
rubric.alternative_methods: R0 decision must identify both genuinely different interpolation methods and give each method's own maximizing permitted coordinate. Grade against independently tabulated interpolated values from the initial observations.
rubric.next_experiment: The accepted R0 decision must precede the new Job and map its chosen candidate IDs and coordinates to the completed follow-up Job and immutable observations.
rubric.held_out: Recompute the measured comparison from the second Job. The winning submitted candidate must have the better score. Require a final reason reporting the observed direction and its finite scope.
rubric.independent_review: A real accepted review and a separate decision-worker submission must refer to the observed proposal and the same frozen evidence. Reviewer must differ from proposal author. Keep scripted and real-provider results independently identified.
rubric.interpretive_review: An independent reader checks the rationales for causal source use, measured contradiction, method-to-candidate mapping, observed head-to-head result, and limitations. Factual disagreement, unacknowledged source, inferred global superiority and a planned but unexecuted experiment are failures. State which dimensions the evidence permits to score.
